title.narrative: El Nino Preparedness Assessment Planning- Kenya & Uganda 2015

description.narrative:
With the predictions of an El Nino phenomenon in Kenya and the South and East African Region, there is need for a preparedness plan for CAFOD and the Caritas Network in Kenya and Uganda. As of November 2015, Most of the CAFOD partners in Northern Kenya had developed contingency plans for a possible El Nino response. Caritas Kenya has already initiated discussions within Kenya to discuss the planning as well as on deliberations for a possible El Nino Appeal .
No concrete decisions have been made so far although discussions with Rome have been going on. CAFOD has actively been represented and participated in these meetings.This being a quick onset emergency and understanding that our reaction times to response needs to be ramped up, our preparedness and response planning requires even higher level of preparedness and planning. At the current time, no appeals have been issued although for CAFOD, the importance of informing our supporters about the impending crisis is can not be over emphasized. Carrying out assessments at this time and stage in the crisis will place us at a better position to provide value added data and field level data to any calls for RRFs applications as well as START funding that requires participating organizations to have some prior understanding of the situation and up-to-date actual field level assessment information. Thus assessment information is paramount and indispensable to a successful application as well as to enhance our capacity and ability to provide timely and targeted response in our strategic geographic areas.
To realise this , there is need to constitute assessment teams to carry out flood risks assessments as well as identify any large affected populations that have not yet been reported by the press in our main areas of work in both Kenya and Uganda.
